description:
Read a destination's configuration, state, and most recent delivery results.

See the [OpenTelemetry export guide](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/opentelemetry#delivery-and-health) to learn how the API delivers spans and when it disables a destination.

AnthropicBeta.description:
Beta names you can send in the `anthropic-beta` header.

See [Beta headers](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/beta-headers) for how to send them and where to find the name a feature needs.

BetaTelemetryDestination.description: An OpenTelemetry destination: an OTLP/HTTP endpoint, the request headers sent with every delivery to it, what the exported spans contain, and which workspaces it covers. A destination belongs to an organization. A workspace's spans go to every enabled destination that covers it.

delivery_health.description: The most recent delivery results for this destination.

display_name.description: Human-readable name for the destination. Null when none was set.

endpoint_url.description:
The base URL of the destination's OTLP/HTTP endpoint, exactly as registered.

The API appends the per-signal path, such as `/v1/traces`, on delivery, unless `traces.endpoint_url` is set.

header_names.description: Names of the registered request headers. Header values are write-only and are never returned.

id.description: The unique ID of the destination (`tdst_...`).

traces.description: The destination's settings for the traces it receives.

updated_at.description:
Time of the last change to the destination's configuration or state. Changes to `delivery_health` don't change it.

An update that sets a header value always changes it, even when the value is the same as before. Adding or removing a single workspace on the destination's list doesn't change it. An update that changes the list does.

workspaces.description: Which of the organization's workspaces the destination covers.

BetaTelemetryDestinationDeliveryHealth.description:
The most recent delivery results that the API records for a telemetry destination.

Changes to the destination's configuration or state don't reset these fields. Changes to these fields don't change `updated_at`. The values can lag behind the latest deliveries.

See the [OpenTelemetry export guide](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/opentelemetry#delivery-and-health) to learn how the API delivers spans and when it disables a destination.

last_error.description:
A message that describes the most recent failed delivery to the destination, or `null` if no delivery has failed yet.

Examples are `temporary DNS failure`, `TLS failure`, `timeout`, `connection failure`, `invalid address`, `HTTP error (status 503)`, and `redirect (status 301)`. The message is `invalid address` both for a hostname that doesn't exist and for an address that isn't publicly routable. It never contains the endpoint's response body, a header value, a network address, or TLS details.

`last_error` and `last_error_at` always change together. A later successful delivery doesn't clear them. If `last_success_at` is later than `last_error_at`, a delivery has succeeded since this failure.

See the [OpenTelemetry export guide](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/opentelemetry#delivery-errors) to learn the likely cause of each error.

last_error_at.description: Time of the failure that `last_error` describes. Changes together with `last_error`. Null until a delivery first fails.

last_success_at.description: Time of the most recent successful delivery to the destination, or `null` if no delivery has succeeded yet.

BetaTelemetryDestinationState.description:
Whether a telemetry destination receives deliveries.

A caller can set either state. The API also disables an enabled destination on its own in some cases. The `reason` of the disabled state says whether a caller or the API disabled the destination and, when the API did, why.

See the [OpenTelemetry export guide](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/opentelemetry#delivery-and-health) to learn when the API disables a destination.

BetaTelemetryDestinationTraces.description: A telemetry destination's settings for the traces it receives.

enabled.description: Whether the destination receives traces. A destination whose `enabled` is false keeps its other settings.

endpoint_url.description:
The full URL that the API posts traces to, exactly as registered, or `null` if the destination doesn't have one.

When it is `null`, the API posts traces to `endpoint_url` with `/v1/traces` appended.

max_content_bytes.description:
The most bytes of content that one exported span can contain, or `null` if only the API's maximum applies.

Content means model prompts and responses, and tool inputs and outputs. The API shortens longer content to this size before it delivers the span. A destination whose `content_mode` is `metadata_only` keeps this value. It applies once `content_mode` is `content`.

BetaTelemetryDestinationWorkspaces.description:
Which of the organization's workspaces a telemetry destination covers.

Several destinations can cover the same workspace. Each of them receives the workspace's spans while it is enabled.

The workspace list of an `include` or `exclude` destination isn't part of the destination object. List the destination's workspaces to read it. Add or remove one workspace at a time, or replace the whole list with an update. A list holds at most 1,000 workspaces.

BetaTelemetryDestinationStateEnabled.description: The telemetry destination receives the spans of the workspaces that it covers.

BetaTelemetryDestinationStateDisabled.description:
The API doesn't deliver anything to the telemetry destination.

Spans produced while it is disabled aren't delivered later.

reason.description: Whether a caller or the API disabled the destination and, when the API did, why. Read-only.

BetaTelemetryDestinationContentMode.description:
What the spans that the API exports to a telemetry destination contain.

See the [OpenTelemetry export guide](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/opentelemetry#choose-a-content-mode) to learn what the spans contain in each content mode.

BetaTelemetryDestinationWorkspacesAll.description: The destination covers every workspace of the organization, including the default workspace, archived workspaces, and workspaces created later. It doesn't have a list.

BetaTelemetryDestinationWorkspacesInclud.description: The destination covers the workspaces on its list, and no others.

BetaTelemetryDestinationWorkspacesExclud.description: The destination covers every workspace of the organization except the workspaces on its list. A workspace created later is covered until it is added to the list.

BetaTelemetryDestinationDisabledReason.description: Why the destination is disabled: `caller` when a caller disabled it, or the reason the API disabled it automatically (`sustained_failure`, `invalid_address`, or `redirect`). Every automatic disable is reversible with an update that sets `state` to `enabled`. An update that sets `disabled` on a destination that is already disabled keeps its reason.

BetaTelemetryDestinationDisabledReasonCa.description: A caller disabled the destination with an update that set `state` to `disabled`.

BetaTelemetryDestinationDisabledReasonSu.description: The API disabled the destination because deliveries to it failed, with no successful delivery in between, for longer than a threshold that Anthropic configures and that is not part of this contract. The reason is `invalid_address` instead when the most recent failed delivery failed with an invalid address.

BetaTelemetryDestinationDisabledReasonIn.description: The API disabled the destination because deliveries to it failed for longer than the same threshold as for `sustained_failure`, and the most recent failed delivery failed with an invalid address: the DNS answer says that the endpoint's hostname doesn't exist or doesn't have an address, or the address that the API would connect to isn't publicly routable or is reserved, for example a loopback, link-local, private-network, or cloud-metadata address. The API doesn't connect to such an address, and retries the delivery a bounded number of times as it does after a timeout. A timeout or a server failure of the DNS lookup is a temporary DNS failure instead, not an invalid address.

BetaTelemetryDestinationDisabledReasonRe.description: The API disabled the destination because the endpoint answered a delivery with a 3xx status. Redirects are never followed, and one such answer disables the destination at once.
